abstract: Maintains magnetic sensor sensitivities and magnetic gradiometry survey track specifications
system_message:
You are Electromagnetic diagnostics lead (EMAG). The Electromagnetic diagnostics lead (EMAG) maintains specifications and records regarding magnetic sensor sensitivities, magnetic gradiometry survey track lengths, and induced low-frequency tone injection parameters across subsea cable fault localization candidates.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Induced tone tracking（INDC）
information_points.content:
EMAG-INDC-T7F：For the Autonomous underwater vehicle acoustic profiling protocol, terminal station bench testing on the armor-grounded sheath circuit indicates a low-frequency tone injection signal strength of 35 mA at 25 Hz.
EMAG-INDC-ALL：For the Towed multi-sensor synthetic aperture protocol, injection tests on the armor-grounded sheath circuit register a low-frequency tone injection signal strength of 15 mA for the 25 Hz injected tracking signal.
EMAG-INDC-748：For the Work-class remotely operated vehicle electric field protocol, the 25 Hz tracking signal on the armor-grounded sheath circuit demonstrates a low-frequency tone injection signal strength of 25 mA.

information_points.title: Maintains magnetic sensor sensitivities and magnetic gradiometry survey track specifications（FLUX）
information_points.content:
EMAG-FLUX-JV3：For the Autonomous underwater vehicle acoustic profiling protocol, the subsea sensor head array achieves a magnetic anomaly detection sensitivity of 0.3 nT based on the RMS noise floor across ambient geomagnetic background, and its planned cumulative linear track for close-range magnetic gradient tracking across the armored cable alignment fault zone establishes a magnetic gradiometry survey line length of 65 km.
EMAG-FLUX-S2J：For the Towed multi-sensor synthetic aperture protocol, calibration records show a magnetic anomaly detection sensitivity of 0.3 nT across the subsea sensor head array against the ambient geomagnetic background, alongside a planned magnetic gradiometry survey line length of 50 km for close-range magnetic gradient tracking along the armored cable fault zone.
EMAG-FLUX-MN4：For the Work-class remotely operated vehicle electric field protocol, the RMS noise floor of the subsea sensor head array yields a magnetic anomaly detection sensitivity of 0.9 nT, while the planned close-range gradient tracking across the armored cable alignment fault zone sets the magnetic gradiometry survey line length at 65 km.
